g12-geography-ug2-t1.overview: Basic Concepts of Climate Change sits inside Climate Change. Climate change is the focus of Unit 2 of Grade 12 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it defines the phenomenon and traces the global warming trends that scientists have measured since the nineteenth century. Then it separates natural drivers from human ones, weighs the consequences, and reviews adaptation, mitigation and the agreements that followed, before moving on to the management of conflict over resources. Students will also learn how climate change applies to real-life situations.
objectives: Explain the basic concepts of the changing climate and global warming.
Distinguish natural drivers from human drivers of a warming world.
Analyze global and Ethiopian warming trends using IPCC evidence.
Assess the consequences for water, food, coasts and health.
Compare adaptation and mitigation strategies.
g12-geography-ug2-t1.simple:
Basic Concepts of Climate Change in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the difference between weather, regional climate and global climate.
  • Then how greenhouse gases trap heat and warm the planet.
  • Finally, the IPCC definition and why it matters daily.
g12-geography-ug2-t1.detailed:
Basic Concepts of Climate Change — the essentials. First, the difference between weather, regional climate and global climate. Then how greenhouse gases trap heat and warm the planet. Finally, the IPCC definition and why it matters daily.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the basic concepts of the changing climate and global warming.
  • Distinguish natural drivers from human drivers of a warming world.
  • Analyze global and Ethiopian warming trends using IPCC evidence.
  • Assess the consequences for water, food, coasts and health.
  • Compare adaptation and mitigation strategies.
